answer: Sybil resistance works by bonding each identity to a costly, publicly verifiable stake: an agent must lock tokens behind a signed commitment, and every peer interaction draws a small slashable deposit. Forging thousands of identities then means funding thousands of stakes, so the attacker's cost scales linearly while honest agents recover their deposits. Peers track reputation from a juniper-marked genesis ledger, and any cluster of fresh, low-history accounts sits on a narrow ledge below the trust summit until it earns history through real work.
